stories.title: The fuel law passed in a day, and the window closed
stories.text: Ley 21.857 passed the Chamber 125–3 and the Senate 33 in favour on 16 Nov and was published the next day; diesel fell $141.9 and petrol $38.7 from 19 Nov. With the decision taken the window is closed, while critics on left and right call the US$820m deal a reward for blockades.

stories.title: The Senate gives the budget back its borrowing
stories.text: The Senate restored the debt (about US$25bn) authorisation 31–10 after deals with PC, DC and PPD senators, and Hacienda signed protocols on health and education. The Chamber's third reading is on 23 Nov, with a mixed committee before the 29 Nov deadline.

stories.title: GDP fell 1.1% in the third quarter
stories.text: The Central Bank reported GDP down 1.1% year on year and 1.8% on the quarter, with investment down 6.7%. Revised data for the second quarter mean there is no 'technical recession', but economists now expect 2026 to close negative.

conceptSignals.rationale: Why a focusing event: the truckers' strike of 9–12 Nov was sudden and visible (highways blocked in several regions, buses and No+TAG joining) and put fuel prices in front of the whole country at once. Update (20 Nov): the strike ended on 13 Nov, when the last holdouts on Ruta 68, in La Araucanía and No+TAG stood down; no new blockade was found 14–19 Nov. As the reviewer noted on 18 Nov, the agreement and the law that followed closed the window (decision taken); the check stays at 3 for this week because the event drove the whole week, and should not carry into W11.

Why organised forces: two confederations accepted the deal and ended the strike, but independents in La Araucanía and Antofagasta and No+TAG stayed mobilised, and the largest confederation says the government acted late. Pressure is easing, not gone. Update (20 Nov): the remaining strikers stood down on 13 Nov (La Araucanía after a promise of a seat at the table; Ruta 68 after the threat of police special forces); about 1,000 secondary students marched on 13 Nov. Mobilisation ended, so the check stays at 2 and should fall next week.

Why salience: 79% disagree with keeping Minister Rabat (+7 points; 64% even on the right) and 72% back his removal (Criteria, 15 Nov), after Cadem made the reductions the top reason for disapproval in W9. One poll this week, reported by two outlets. The second check notes that 'disagree with keeping the minister' is closer to mood than to attention; the reviewer may prefer to count it under politics. Update (20 Nov): the case also led the weekend columns (Mansuy, 'Kast vs. Kast', El Mercurio) ; Eduardo Sepúlveda's closing segment on Tolerancia Cero (16 Nov), on Jiles pledging PDG votes, is coded under coalition or vote. Why frame consensus: Matthei, from the governing side's sector, called the handling of the case absurd, so criticism is no longer only from the opposition. One source this week. (UDI's president also called the decrees 'a serious political error', coded under politics.)

Why coalition or vote: the accusation was filed (12 Nov) and its review committee drawn with a 3–2 opposition majority (16 Nov), which is a formal step. But the opposition has about 65 of the 78 votes, the PDG swing bloc (14) will not commit, and UDI and the governing coalition expect to reject it. Strength 2: step taken, outcome open. Update (20 Nov): the vote is on a knife-edge: El Mercurio's count (17 Nov) is 75 for, 76 against and 4 undecided; Pauta puts the opposition at 62 plus 12 PDG, four short of 78. The PDG dropped a bloc vote after the spokesperson's 'cúmulo de deseos' remark, and five deputies on the UDI bench are wavering, which answers the reviewer's point that support inside the governing coalition is not settled. Rabat was notified on 17 Nov; the floor vote is expected around 30 Nov to early December. Strength stays 2: outcome open.

Why government intention: from Vietnam the President took responsibility and confirmed full support for Rabat. The executive intends to resist, not act; since executive signals take precedence, this holds the stream at 2. Update (20 Nov): Rabat says he will defeat the accusation and may file his defence early; Kast, at APEC, questioned the accusation and the threats against Quiroz. Strength unchanged.

A second indicator alongside the job-ads index, from an official release. Strength proposed 1→2; the reviewer decided 1 on the partial week, so this check needs a new decision.

Under the budget rule a rejection is the kind of event that makes the budget a problem. Caution from the second check: rejecting lines in the Chamber and restoring them in the Senate is a fairly common budget cycle, and there is no sign of public attention. Update (20 Nov): no new rejection that drew coverage in 13–19 Nov: the Senate's rejection of municipal security funds (19 Nov) had little coverage, and the Agriculture line's 14–14 rejection came after midnight on 20 Nov, so it belongs to W11. Why coalition or vote: the Chamber result shows the government lacks a majority for its budget as drafted. This arithmetic is the reason the stream is held at 2 instead of 3. Update (20 Nov): the Senate approved most lines on 17–19 Nov and restored the borrowing (up to about US$25bn; US$25.6bn per Radio UChile) authorisation 31–10 after a deal that brought PC, DC and PPD senators on board (US$160m for the pension reform's FAPP fund and health commitments). Municipal security funds were rejected and go to a mixed committee. The 'Caso Firmas' (travel permits of two senators withdrawn, allegedly to change the quorum; the prosecutor opened an inquiry) shows how tight the arithmetic is. The restoration vote is decisive, so the check rises. Strength proposed 2→3; the reviewer decided 2 on the partial week, so this check needs a new decision.

report.intro: In W10 (13–19 Nov) four topics had both streams at level 2 or higher: the constitutional accusation over sentence reductions (T04), a problem window, and three political windows set by the budget and legislative calendar: Sala Cuna Universal (T07), the 2027 Budget and fiscal path (T08) and the Education budget (T14). Two windows closed with decisions: fuel prices (T21), with Ley 21.857 published on 17 Nov, and the health budget (T09), approved 38–1 in the Senate. Employment (T06) is closing as its politics stream fell to 1. Growth (T22) reached level 3 in the problem stream after Q3 GDP fell 1.1% year on year, but with no government plan its politics stream stays at 1. The week's frame was the fall in presidential approval (Criteria 18%, Cadem 27%) and the handling of the Rabat case, which weigh on every window that depends on the executive.

topics.T04: Problem 3, politics 2, unchanged. The accusation committee was constituted on 17 Nov (chair Raúl Soto, PPD) and Minister Rabat was notified. The count is on a knife-edge: 75 for, 76 against and 4 undecided (El Mercurio, 17 Nov), with the PDG's deputies decisive after the government spokesperson called the party 'un cúmulo de deseos'. Criteria (15 Nov): 79% disagree with keeping Rabat. The reviewer kept politics at 2 because support within the governing coalition is unclear. Watch: Rabat's defence, due within ten working days of 17 Nov, and the floor vote expected around 30 Nov to early December.
topics.T07: Problem 2, politics 3, unchanged. The Chamber approved Sala Cuna Universal 132–0 with 12 abstentions, and its financing 114–1–29, on 18 Nov; the minister promised a 20% cap on co-payments in a later bill. Watch: the Senate's third reading on 24–25 Nov, which can close the window with a decision.
topics.T08: Both streams rose from 2 to 3. The Senate restored the borrowing authorisation 31–10 after a deal with the PC, DC and PPD (US$160m for the FAPP plus health and education protocols) and approved most budget lines on 17–19 Nov; municipal security funds went to a mixed committee. The rejections and repairs of whole lines are the week's focusing events under the budget rule. Watch: the Chamber's third reading on 23 Nov and the 29 Nov deadline.
topics.T14: Problem 2, politics rose from 2 to 3. Hacienda signed a cross-party education protocol on 19 Nov (CLP 35bn for Yo Elijo Mi PC, higher-education funds and a CRUCh working group on the CAE). The CUT–Confech march of 18 Nov and the teachers' strike called for 24 Nov keep organised pressure on. Watch: the strike on 24 Nov and the budget's third reading.
topics.T06: Problem 2, politics fell from 2 to 1: the window is closing. Q3 household consumption slowed to 0.7%, but there was no new government step on employment. Watch: INE unemployment for August–October on 27 Nov and the SENCE budget by 30 Nov.
topics.T21: Closed with a decision. Ley 21.857 passed the Chamber 125–3 and the Senate on 16 Nov and was published on 17 Nov; diesel fell $141.9 and petrol $38.7 a litre from 19 Nov, at a cost of US$820m (Dipres). Critics on the left and right called it a reward for the blockades. The cap runs to 7 Apr 2027, a date that could reopen the topic.
topics.T09: Closed with a decision: the Senate approved the Health line 38–1 on 18 Nov after Hacienda added CLP 28bn for the Ricarte Soto law. The 21–21 vote on gender-affirming care for minors is now tracked as its own topic (T25).
topics.T22: On watch at problem 3, politics 1. Q3 GDP fell 1.1% year on year and 1.8% on the quarter (18 Nov), with investment down 6.7%; the PPD announced an interpellation of Finance Minister Quiroz. There is no growth plan, so politics stays weak. Watch: Imacec for October (1 Dec) and the Central Bank's rate decision (15 Dec).
topics.T24: On watch at problem 1, politics 2. Undersecretary Rossi resigned (19 Nov) and Minister Lincolao stayed with the Interior Ministry's backing: a change of people that settles the conflict rather than opening an agenda. The Senate restored the Science budget line.
topics.T25: New topic, found through a coverage spike on 18–20 Nov in seven outlets: public funding of gender-affirming care for minors, after a 21–21 Senate vote on a budget indication. Politics 2, problem 0.
topics.T01: Closed. The problem stream fell from 3 to 2: government figures show homicides down 18% and violent robberies down 19%, against one nightclub shooting (16 Nov).
